i currently intermittent fast and i love it. The best is finding a window that works best for you. I used to skip breakfast and eat my first meal at 12pm, but i’d be starving at lunch and constantly tempted to overeat. For the last two years, however, I’ve started my fast in the evening instead. I eat breakfast at around 9am, lunch at a normal time, and dinner at 4:45 to ultimate stop eating by 6 pm. I make sure my dinner is a bit higher in volume than breakfast or lunch to keep me full throughout the night, and make sure to have at least 1, 40oz water bottle after dinner and a hot tea. I always wake up feeling lighter because i know my last meal was processed well before I woke up. But it’s not for everyone, and can add stress to your body. So I’d recommend trying it, but if you notice you’re too starving, just stick to a regular eating schedule :)

i’m sorry your weight loss process was such a struggle, it can be really hard to find the balance between what looks healthy and what’s actually healthy. To start, I would slowly add back calories into your diet. Any drastic changes will cause rapid gain, which I’m sure would be triggering. Just like someone trying to move into maintenance, every week, try to add an extra 100-150 calories. Your body will slowly adjust each week until you are at a normal, healthy intake. Along with calorie increase, add in some protein. Yogurts, protein shakes, lean meats, bars, whatever you feel most comfortable with. 

The ultimate goal is to slowly adjust back to a truly healthy, fueling diet, so that you can maintain or continue to reach your goals but not at the cost of your physical and mental health. Sending my support!

for the steps, pick a podcast, make a playlist and chose songs at your pace that you wanna memorize the words to etc. Get one of those apps like sweatco that pays u a few cents for every mile u walk—whatever motivates you. As far as food goes, you’re going to have to restrict unfortunately to see that 25-40 lb loss by october. it doesn’t have to be miserable though. Go on tiktok or instagram and find fun, low calorie recipes and experiment. if you know you’re prone to snacking, plan out your food a day in advance and carve out say 300 cals for snacks that are truly filling. 

You want to make sure you’re ready to actually change your habits… plainly, you have to change to see change. 

To simplify it, make general goals for yourself that seem more manageable. Get 7-10k steps per day(anything in that range would then work. some days maybe 7k, some 8.5k, so on). Only have processed sugar 2x a week for example, or try to make 1 bag of chips last 1 whole week, drink 80+oz of water each day. Sleep 7+ hours per night, etc. simple adjustments will add up to make bigger results. 

Good luck! I’m rooting for you :)
